# `ecommerce_gold_revenue_reconciles`

> Gold revenue matches the silver orders it was built from.

| | |
|---|---|
| Domain | [ecommerce](README.md) |
| Layer | **gold** — evaluated by the `gold` gate |
| Model | `gld_ecommerce__daily_sales` (`ecommerce_gold_staging.gld_ecommerce__daily_sales`) |
| Check | `reconciles_with` |
| Severity | `error` — a violation **stops the pipeline** |
| Defined in | [dbt/models/ecommerce/gold/_gold.yml](../../../dbt/models/ecommerce/gold/_gold.yml) |

## What it checks

`sum(net_revenue)` equals `sum(items_net_total)` of `slv_ecommerce__orders` where `status not in ('cancelled', 'refunded')`, within 0.01.

## When it fails

The `gold` task of `medallion_ecommerce` fails, `publish_gold` doesn't run, and the batch is never added to `ecommerce_gold`: consumers keep the batches published before. `quality_report` marks the run as blocked and sends the alert, if one is configured.

The rows that broke the rule in its latest evaluation are kept in `dq_audit.ecommerce_gold_revenue_reconciles`.

## Tested by

No sample-data scenario trips this rule yet: it guards against cases the generators don't produce.

```sql
-- rows that broke the rule last time it ran
select * from dq_audit.ecommerce_gold_revenue_reconciles;

-- history of the rule
select batch_id, status, failures, recorded_at
from dq_audit.rule_results
where rule = 'ecommerce_gold_revenue_reconciles'
order by recorded_at desc;
```

## Definition

```yaml
reconciles_with:
  expression: sum(net_revenue)
  compare_model: ref('slv_ecommerce__orders')
  compare_expression: sum(items_net_total)
  compare_filter: status not in ('cancelled', 'refunded')
```
